On 2026-05-10, the Primeira Liga spotlight fell on Alverca as they hosted Estoril Praia in an encounter that promised tactical intrigue and high-intensity competition. Both sides took to the pitch with everything to play for, setting the stage for a dramatic afternoon of football. Early Pressure and VAR Drama Alverca began the match with intent, looking to establish dominance from the opening whistle in front of a crowd of 3,031 spectators. The first significant breakthrough occurred in the 12th minute when Lucas Figueiredo capitalized on a precise assist from Nabili Touaizi , slotting the ball home with his left foot. However, celebrations were briefly put on hold for a VAR review. After two minutes of tension, the referee confirmed the goal in the 14th minute, giving the home side the lead. Alverca thought they had doubled their advantage in the 34th minute when Lucas Figueiredo found the net again, but this time the VAR intervention ruled the goal out for offside. As the first half drew to a close, Estoril began to find their rhythm, coming agonizingly close to an equalizer when Yanis Begraoui struck the post with a powerful finish. Instant Response and Tactical Battle The second half saw Estoril Praia introduce Gonçalo Costa and Andre Lacximicant in a double substitution that paid immediate dividends. Just two minutes after the restart, Gonçalo Costa turned provider for Andre Lacximicant , who leveled the score with a clinical left-footed finish. This early strike shifted the momentum, allowing Estoril to control more of the ball, eventually reaching 58% possession as they searched for a winner. In the final stages, the match became increasingly physical, marked by tactical fouls and a flurry of yellow cards for Bastien Meupiyou , Kaiky Naves , and Pedro Carvalho . Despite late pressure and a missed chance by Pedro Carvalho in stoppage time, neither side could find a decisive blow. The final whistle confirmed a hard-fought draw, a result that felt fair given the balanced nature of the contest.

The Primeira Liga encounter between Famalicao and Alverca on May 16, 2026, was a testament to defensive discipline and tactical patience. Both sides entered the pitch with clear structures, knowing that a single error could define their afternoon in this closely contested league battle. A Tactical Stalemate in the Opening Half The match began with a cautious rhythm as both teams felt each other out in the early exchanges. Famalicao attempted to use their home advantage, with Gustavo Sa delivering several corners in the first few minutes, though the Alverca defense remained resolute. The first sign of tension came in the 20th minute when Nabili Touaizi was forced into a tactical foul to halt a counter-attack, earning himself a yellow card. Alverca responded through the set-piece delivery of Chiquinho , but neither side could find the clinical edge required to break the deadlock before the interval. Substitutions and a Shift in Momentum As the second half progressed, the managers began to look toward their benches for a spark. Famalicao made a decisive move in the 64th minute, bringing on Umar Abubakar for Simon Elisor . The game remained stretched, with both Sorriso and Chiquinho being flagged for offside as they tried to beat the defensive lines. Tensions rose again when Tommie van de Looi saw yellow for a shirt-pull, but the tactical chess match continued until the final ten minutes of regulation time. Abubakar's Header Breaks the Deadlock The defining moment arrived in the 83rd minute. After a period of sustained pressure, Rafa Soares delivered a pinpoint cross into the heart of the box. The substitute Umar Abubakar rose highest to meet the ball, powering a header home to send the home fans into raptures. Despite Alverca throwing players forward and Chiquinho receiving a late booking for a reckless challenge, Famalicao managed the closing stages with a series of tactical substitutions to secure the victory as the referee blew the final whistle at 90+4 minutes.
